svg.title: Noor painted face reference
svg.text: Noor: painted face reference
For the TA's v2 style frames: stroke direction on the face, how strokes break at the edges, painted darks. Same rules as style-guide.md sections 3–5.
THE QUIET CAR · character design · v1
A STROKE DIRECTION ON THE FACE
Forehead: across, curving down at the temples.
Temples and side planes: down the side of the head.
Eye zone: along the lids and the socket.
Nose: down the ridge. Cheeks: down and in, from the
cheekbone toward the mouth corner, turning along the jaw.
Upper lip: short and near-vertical. Chin: around the form.
Hair: along the sweep, back toward the bun (not strands).
Strokes are locked to the surface (UV/object space).
B PAINTED STUDY: 3/4, ASLEEP-CAR TOP LIGHT
C HOW STROKES BREAK AT THE EDGES
LIT EDGE: firm. Where a form faces the panel, its
edge against the background stays crisp.
TERMINATOR: light-to-shadow breaks into strokes
2–3 wide, driven by the real light. It moves when the light moves.
SHADOW EDGE: lost. As the form turns away, the
edge softens and merges with the dark behind it.
Facial features are always firm; they are the last thing the shadow takes.
D PAINTED DARKS: NOOR'S SKIN FROM LIT PLANE TO TRUE BLACK
lit plane
top planes facing the panel: forehead,
cheekbone tops, nose ridge, lower lip,
chin top
halftone
her albedo: planes turning away
terminator
where strokes break up: 2–3 strokes wide
(~1–1.5 cm on her face)
core shadow
cooler and greyer: grey-green bounce off
the teal and laminate, never red
shadow in near-dark
strokes merge into larger, quieter
shapes; chroma drops
true black
0,0,0: no texture, no grain, no lift
These are albedo/value targets for reading, NOT colours to paint into textures: the real light produces them. Two build suggestions for a stronger painted look that stay physically lit:
(1) Planes in the geometry: give the face soft planar facets (forehead, temple, cheek front/side, jaw, nose sides) so the panel light lays down painter's planes by itself.
(2) Darks merge: blend a larger Kuwahara kernel into the low-luminance areas (a luminance mask), so shadows become bigger, quieter shapes while lit features stay crisp. Blackout stays 0.
